tasks.title: ORSet resurrection and LWWMap get/value
requirements: MV-CRDT-01: ORSet remove keeps observed-remove information so a stale replica cannot resurrect a removed element (A adds, B syncs, A removes, A syncs with B's old state). (source: owner notes of 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md:24; baseline 8.5)
MV-CRDT-02: LWWMap.get and LWWMap.value agree after an older delete is merged with a newer write. (source: owner notes of 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md:25; baseline 8.5)

ORSet.remove and remove_tag record the observed tags as tombstones and merge takes the union of tombstones, so a stale replica cannot bring a removed element back; add-wins against a concurrent unobserved add is unchanged (source: crdt-merge CHANGELOG.md entry of this branch; tests/test_orset_lwwmap_correctness.py:45 for the stale replica and :194 for the older delete merged with a newer write; programme task WP01-01)

tasks.title: TrustAgentState delete is a replicated observed-remove
requirements: MV-CRDT-04: TrustAgentState delete is a replicated tombstone and its merge is observed-remove/causal; it is not called production-grade until then. (source: owner notes of 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md:27; baseline 8.5)

tasks.title: Contribution tags are globally unique and survive a round trip
requirements: MV-CRDT-06: Operation and contribution tags are globally unique ((node id, counter) or UUID) and equal-timestamp LWW and FWW ties are order independent. (source: owner notes of 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md:29; baseline 8.5)

CRDTMergeState contribution tags carry a random 128-bit id and are serialised with each contribution, so a remove in one process cannot tombstone an unrelated add in another and tombstones keep matching after to_dict and from_dict (source: crdt-merge CHANGELOG.md entry of this branch; tests/test_crdt_state_tag_uniqueness.py:44, :51 and :71; programme task WP01-05)
